A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAMM research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across renumbering. Internal reporting inconsistencies in v3 do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original C4 pretraining, PAMM finetuning on GLUE, throughput measurements, compression ablations and activation/gradient analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds LLaMA-7B pretraining, Pixtral-12B finetuning on AID, batch/sequence-length ablations and operation-level timing results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same generator sampling, assignment, scaling and approximate-backpropagation procedure. The LoRA experiment applies this existing compressor to adapter inputs; it does not introduce a new PAMM algorithm component.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates language-model pretraining on C4 and language understanding on GLUE. v3 retains these and adds AID satellite-image classification using Pixtral-12B with images and textual prompts across 30 classes (Section 4.7), substantially extending coverage into vision-language tasks.

E2.justification: CompAct and Uniform-CRS remain unchanged in the compression comparison, and the existing full-memory controls are retained. New Table 4 evaluates pretrained Pixtral and LoRA-only finetuning against LoRA+PAMM, adding comparator configurations absent from v2's experiments.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 revises the stated throughput protocol from 16K-token batches on one GPU to tokens/second/GPU with a 128K-token global batch and eight-GPU DDP for 1B/7B. New experiments introduce seven batch/sequence-length configurations, 150K-step 7B training, and rank-128 LoRA with macro/weighted F1 evaluation. Memory accounting now explicitly includes coefficients and assignment indices. The revised descriptions do not establish that retained throughput entries were rerun.

E4.justification: New Section 4.5 tests sensitivity to batch size and sequence length against the baseline. Appendix F adds detailed operation profiling and reports that reusing generators brought no speed gain and slightly degraded perplexity. The existing rank/epsilon ablation, compression-error analyses and loss-stability plots are retained.

E5.justification: Retained experiments keep their three-run/three-seed averaging, error bars and ± reporting. The added Pixtral comparison also uses three runs and reports standard deviations, extending the existing uncertainty-reporting approach. No increased replication count or new statistical testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Substantial new results cover 7B training, Pixtral-LoRA, batch/length sensitivity and operation timing. Table 6 reports final 7B perplexity of 13.57 for PAMM-512 versus 14.61 for the baseline; Table 4 reports macro F1 of 0.9727 for PAMM-128 versus 0.9711 for LoRA alone. v2 Table 3 becomes v3 Table 5, with unchanged perplexities but increased memory estimates, including 18 to 24 MB for 1B at r=1/512. Runtime results are replaced/expanded under revised reporting settings. Figure 3 and Table 6 show different 7B PAMM orderings without explaining the difference.

T1.justification: New Appendix J adds a supplementary complexity derivation: storage kn+2b, an operation-cost expression simplified to O(kn(b+m)), and the theoretical speedup ratio bm/[k(b+m)]. The existing mathematical definitions, approximation bounds, Lemmas 1–2 and their proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the headline factor of up to 512 from reducing projection memory consumption to compressing projection activations, narrowing what the factor describes. The central claims about PAMM, preserved model quality and composability remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix J qualifies theoretical speedup through GPU memory movement and kernel-launch overhead; v2 instead explicitly dismissed substantial benefits from a custom CUDA kernel. Section 4.7 explains the limited benefit of compressing LoRA's B-layer inputs, and Section 4.5 interprets the new batch/length results as robustness. Existing FlashAttention limitations and discussion of large gradient-approximation errors remain.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the 7B training budget, GPU count, scaling factor and learning-rate grid; it also specifies LoRA rank, affected model branches and generator counts. Appendix F newly discloses tree-reduction argmax and explicitly describes per-step sampling. The original pseudocode, existing training details and supplementary-code availability statement are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Pixtral (Agrawal et al., 2024) and AID (Xia et al., 2017) for the new evaluation. Section 2 and the positioning relative to attention approximations, activation compression and approximate backpropagation remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact. v3 adds experimental and complexity subsections, renames the existing ablation subsection, renumbers retained appendices, revises the throughput paragraph and changes the publication header. These are localized structural and language edits.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn to include 7B and display two PAMM ratios instead of three; the omitted r=1/128 results remain in Appendix D. Table 2b replaces operation-runtime columns with forward/backward/total throughput rows. New tables organize batch/length ablations, multimodal results, 7B checkpoints and operation breakdowns. Other existing figures are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, broader experiments provide useful support for scalability, LoRA compatibility and sensitivity to batch/sequence length. Including coefficient/index storage also improves the credibility of memory accounting. However, unexplained differences between the 7B plot and Table 6, conflicting 1B/7B runtime labels, and the mismatch between Appendix F's sampling-time claim and Table 7 weaken the added evidence. The net quality gain is positive but limited.
